test_focus: N=30 confirmation of Phase 21's per-prompt content routing finding. P21's CI [38%, 57%] was wide and straddled 50%. P26 doubles the N to halve the CI width.
tester: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context), live as the developer

experiment_design.scenario_mix: 3 debugging + 2 decision-shaped + 2 creative-shape (same set as P21)
arms: static — no content routing, sample from full mixed archive
routed — per-prompt content routing via keyword classifier, sample by category filter
experiment_design.archives: Both arms get the same mixed archive: 3 engineering-craft + 3 myth dreams.
experiment_design.wrapper: Both arms use neutral wrapper. Only the seed CATEGORY differs.

aggregate.interpretation: Per-prompt content routing genuinely LOSES at N=210. Lower CI bound 33.6%, upper bound 46.7% — ENTIRELY below 50%. Static routing wins by ~10 percentage points.

phase_21_vs_26_comparison.interpretation: P21 at N=105 reported 47.6% with CI [38%, 57%] — straddling 50%. P26 at N=210 reports 40% with CI [34%, 47%] — fully below 50%. The point estimate shifted DOWN (toward worse) as the CI tightened. P21 was at the optimistic edge of the noise band; the truth is closer to 40% routed-win-rate.

implications: **Per-prompt content routing (keyword classifier) actively HURTS outcomes.** Routing reduces dream variety by filtering — the static arm's diverse-sampling beats the routed arm's filtered-sampling even on debugging prompts where the classifier correctly picks EC seeds.

**The hypothesis isn't classifier-precision — it's filtering-vs-diversity.** Even on debugging (where the keyword classifier correctly identifies engineering and picks EC), the routed arm at 39% [30%, 49%] loses to the static arm's mixed sampling. The diverse dreams archive (some EC, some myth) appears to inadvertently work better than category-filtered sampling.

**Decision-shaped is the worst case for routing.** Routed wins only 33% [23%, 46%] on decision prompts. The keyword classifier flips these to creative → myth seeds, but an engineering-styled agent with neutral wrapper doesn't benefit from myth seeds; the mixed static archive does better.

**Creative scenarios are roughly tied.** Routed 48% [36%, 61%] vs static — straddles 50%. The agent's voice is engineering; injecting myth-only seeds doesn't recreate Phase 11's creative-agent + dreams magic.
**Shipping decision: keep `use_content_routing=False` as default.** The Phase 21 hint is now confirmed. Per-prompt content routing as currently implemented should NOT be enabled.
**Phase 27 will test whether LLM classification fixes this.** The hypothesis is no (since the issue is filtering not accuracy), but worth measuring.

feature_verdicts.per_prompt_content_routing_keyword_class: actively hurts — 40% win rate, CI fully below 50%
feature_verdicts.p21_interpretation_revised: P21's 47.6% was the upper edge of the noise band; P26's tighter measurement shows true rate is ~40%.

known_limitations: Phase 26 confirms Phase 21's mechanism doesn't pay off. The keyword classifier's accuracy is one possible cause — Phase 27 tests this.
The 'filter reduces diversity' hypothesis is intuitive but not directly tested. A future phase could compare routed-pure-EC vs routed-pure-myth vs static-mixed at fixed N.
verdict: CLARIFYING NEGATIVE — per-prompt content routing should NOT be enabled by default. The N=210 measurement resolves Phase 21's wide CI; the keyword-classifier-driven routing genuinely loses to static.
next_steps: Phase 27 (running): does the LLM classifier (Phase 19/27) change the outcome? If yes, the issue was accuracy. If no, the issue is filtering-vs-diversity.
Phase 28: telemetry exporter for cross-deployment analysis (no LLM cost).
Phase 31 (suggested): diversity-vs-routing experiment — three arms: pure-EC, pure-myth, mixed. Confirm that mixing wins regardless of prompt shape.
